newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 9.

text.p: Following were the leading stories in Sri Lankan newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Sri Lanka air force, which has lost about 20 aircraft and helicopters during the last two years, considers purchase of new planes, senior military official says.
Police uncover 32 shotguns and pistols from the office of a left-wing trade union in Colombo and take two people into custody for questioning.
Sri Lanka to receive $14.8 million from the World Bank to strengthen its institutional and policy framework for environmental management and conservation.

The main opposition United National Party (UNP) working committee on Tuesday approved an agreement signed between government and UNP leaders last week to cooperate on issues aimed at ending Sri Lanka's 13-year-old ethnic war.

Some 1,700 government medical officers to call an islandwide 24-hour token strike on Thursday in protest of salary anomalies. Railway workers also threaten strike on Thursday if governent fails to find a satisfactory solution to their demands for higher pay.
Sri Lanka's Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte calls for a terrorism-free 21st century while adressing a Pacific Armies Management seminar held in Hawaii.
Railway workers and government doctors to strike on Thursday, claiming their demands for rectifying salary anomalies not being looked into by government
